description: A pure CALCULATION node — classify a graph's branches into a road hierarchy and split them onto three outputs: Longest, Secondary, Tertiary. Draws nothing on canvas.
instructions:
A value-only node: one graph in as JSON, THREE graphs out as JSON (one per tier). No geometry input or output; draws nothing on the canvas.

WHAT IT DOES: hierarchical branch ordering of a tree-like graph (a skeleton / medial axis), like a Strahler / stream order for a road network. Working per connected component, it peels the single longest route through the component (its weighted diameter) — that trunk is the LONGEST tier. Removing it lets the branches that hung off the trunk fall out as their own pieces; the longest route of each is a SECONDARY branch. Everything left (branches off the secondaries, and deeper) is TERTIARY.

INPUT: graph takes { "nodes": [{ "id", "x", "y" }, ...], "edges": [{ "from_node_id", "to_node_id" }, ...] } — coordinates in metres, local to the anchor. Wire Skeleton's val-branches (best after a Sampled Voronoi skeleton, which stays connected) or Graph Geometry's val-graph into valin-graph. For a single main spine rather than one-per-fragment, feed a CONNECTED graph (e.g. Graph Reduce -> Largest Component first).

OUTPUTS: val-longest, val-secondary and val-tertiary each publish that tier's edges as a graph in the same shape. Typical use — wire each output into its own Set Thickness (wide trunk, medium secondary, thin tertiary), then Merge Graph -> Mitered Join to stroke a hierarchical road network in one pass.
